Rolex Murder

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How not to investigate a murder - a masterclass by Sandton police

Unique Selling Point:
Exclusive interview with widow who witnessed her husband's murder.
Video footage of the incident

Summary:
Pete & Nicola Hoffman lived in Durban. They were on business in Sandton on 26 February 2018, staying at the Hydro Executive Suites. They had dinner at Trumps in Nelson Mandela Square, where Pete posted it on Facebook.
At 10.20pm they paid the bill and left the restaurant to drive back to their hotel in Grayston Drive. As they drove into the parking garage at 10:39pm they noticed there were no security guards on duty, and the boom was up - highly irregular for 24/7 security. They drove to the back of the underground parking, to the last parking next to the lifts. Pete reversed the Mercedes Benz Vito into the parking. As they opened their doors to get out a white Mercedes Benz sedan followed them into the garage and stopped a few metres away with its lights on. Three men got out carrying guns. Two of them ran up to Pete and shot him 7 times and stole his Rolex watch, gun and holster.t.
A resident who heard the shots called SAPS and the ambulance.
The security guards arrived on the scene 20 minutes later.
Nic is now suing 24/7 security for R43 million.

12 days after Pete’s murder, on 7th March 2018, a special operation combining SAPS, Big Boyz Security and JMPD arrested a gang of armed robbers who had just hit a Clicks store in Midstream. The three men were arrested and taken to Midrand Police Station.
The suspects in Midrand CAS 171/03/2018
1. Vusi Msimango
2. Sandile Skhosana
3. Tumelo Madubu
On 9 March the suspects were fetched by Alexandra SAPS task team and taken to their homes in Alex, where a task team found 3 Rolex watches, a gun and holster, a Mercedes Benz key. A photograph was sent to Nicola of the stash – she recognized Pete’s watch – stopped at the exact time the murder took place – 10h40. When she later went to Alexandra SAPS, then Sandton SAPS to identify the watch, they brought out a different watch.





Further information:
The Cover-Up

1. Sandton CAS 847/02/2018 is registered on the SAPS system as Robbery with Firearm. NO mention of Murder. This is done to massage crime statistics according to Captain Ben Booysen.
2. Forensic Officer gave sworn statement on 29 June 2018 that the body under CAS 847/02/2018 known as Body 412/2018 was identified by Tersia Robbetze as the body of Marten Koekemoer. But Koekemoer died and was cremated in Nov 2017.
3. SAPS officer not present at post-mortem. Bullets not collected for 5 months, subsequently lost, so no ballistics. 5 months to collect bullets found in bonnet of car by panel beater. But where are they?
4. No 205 done on Nicole’s phone for 7 months. Located in Limpopo, but never collected. Vodacom confirms the phone is still active.
5. No video footage collected from Trumps; only partial video footage 20” collected from Hydro, the remainder was wiped;
6. When Nicole contacted Peter Machlup, the 2nd hand Rolex dealer for a valuation of Pete’s watch he claimed to have no record of it. She subsequently found the invoice. Some of the Rolex Submariner’s advertised on his website do not have papers. So where does he get them from?


2 Years Later

The docket has been with Detective Hennie Last since October 2018. Nicole thought he was with the Hawks. He is actually now a member of the Narcotics Unit.
Nicole has written to Gauteng Provincial Commissioner 3 x asking for assistance. No reply.

Script:


ROLEX MURDER


V/O: Durban couple Piet and Nicole Hoffmann were in Sandton on business last year.

Nicole: When Piet said goodbye to his daughter he, we didn’t think he wasn’t coming back.

V/O: It was the 26th of February. They had dinner at Trump’s Grill in Nelson Mandela Square, before heading back to their hotel in Grayston Drive. Unbeknown to them, they were being followed. As they turned into the Hydro Park Executive Suites a white Mercedes Benz was on their tail.

Nicole: They drove in straight in here. So we went all the way round the carpark and reversed in here, and they drove straight up here and came running and shot us in there.

V/O: Ex-policeman Piet was armed but was only able to fire one shot into the floor of his own vehicle.

Derek: Nicole what did you see?

Nicole: I saw two people running towards us. The person that ran towards me had a balaclava on, but I could see his eyes, and his nose and his mouth. And I dived underneath the dashboard, curled up into a ball and shut my eyes. and sounded like automatic weapon was bup bup, bup, bup, bup, bup, bup and extremely loud. He had screamed and climbed out the car and then I heard that it went quiet and I heard voices and then somebody walked towards my side and buckled the door back. The car was not drivable after that they actually physically buckled it back grabbed me and robbed me of my jewellery my handbag. And I kept my eyes closed and I just played dead and then they left.

V/O: Piet was shot 7 times and died instantly.

Nicole: And then I went to call Piet, and he was lying on the floor. And then I ran for help, and I was screaming for help and there was nobody, there was no security, there was no one in the car park.

V/O: The killers stole Piet’s gun and holster and his silver Rolex watch. Hydro Park is a residential block of flats, but some units are also rented out as executive hotel suites. Today security is tight - with electronic booms and guards – but on the night of the murder there was just an open, manual boom with no guards in sight.

Derek: Security is tight today, but at that time apparently there was no security?

Will: There was, but not as a reaction unit so to speak.

Derek: But Will, they drove in. The booms were up?

Will: They followed them. I understand that.

V/O: Will Wallis is the Hydro Park Facilities Manager.

Derek: How many incidents of armed robbery have taken place right here in the garage?

Will: In the garage - there were two.

V/O: But in addition to Piet’s murder, we have security camera footage of three other armed robberies in the garage.

Sfx: Blah, blah firearm.

V/O: In two of the cases you can see the security guards beating a hasty retreat.

Will: We’ve replaced the security company, we’ve put in new cameras, we’ve put in booms.

V/O: Two weeks after Piet’s murder there was a breakthrough. A joint task team arrested 3 armed suspects in Midrand after they robbed a Click’s store. Sandile Skhosana, Vusi Msimango, and Thumelo Mobudu are career criminals. Between them they’ve been arrested 30 times in the last decade.

Link: The three suspects arrested in Midrand were brought to Alexandra township by the task force to search their homes. It was here they found evidence which Nicole believes links them to the murder of her husband.

Nicole: I looked at the picture and I said that looks like my husband’s watch. It was even stopped on the time of his death – twenty to eleven – and a Rolex stops 48 hours after you take it off your arm.

Derek: What did you see in that photo?

Nicole: Two other watches, a holster, a Mercedes key, some bullets and underneath was written Hydro Executive Suites murder.

V/O: But when Nicole went to identify the watch at Sandton police station, she was shown a different watch.

Nicole: It was a silver and gold Rolex with the blue face. I showed him a picture of my husband’s silver submariner with a black face. I was told that all the watches that had been recovered from Skhosana’s house were fakes.

Derek: So what do you think happened to Piet’s watch.

Nicole: Nobody knows; the police say they don’t know.

V/O: Law enforcement expert Lobo das Neves finds this inexcusable.

Lobo: That incident is bizarre. The mere fact that there’s evidence, that an exhibit was recovered and photographed, identified - well provisionally identified - and then lost. There is no excuse for that.

V/O: A month later someone called her claiming to be from Crime Intelligence.

W/O: I’m looking into a matter where the watch of your husband was swapped.

Nicole: Well, we don’t know for a fact that it was his watch, but it looked like his watch, and yes definitely the watches that are there now, are not the same watch.

W/O: The thing is, I’m looking more into the corruption matter of the police members.

V/O: Brigadier Mathapelo Peters is the provincial police spokesperson.

Brigadier: The only thing I’m prepared to say at this stage is that there is a bigger project, over and above this one investigation, which are looking into certain commonalities – be it the robbery, where Rolexes are involved. So, we do not want to jeopardize this project. It’s big.

Link: According to police crime statistics 58 people are murdered every day in South Africa. That means by next Sunday another 406 people will lose their lives. It’s a shocking reality, but what if the true figure is actually higher? What if all murders are not recorded as murders?

V/O: A few months after Piet’s death Nicole phoned Sandton police station for some information.

Nicole: And I said to her CAS 847, my husband’s murder. And she said but 847 case is not a murder. It’s registered as a robbery.

Brigadier: Well from the information that we have Derek, two charges were registered on the case on the same day, just a minute apart. It was a robbery with firearm as well as a murder case.

Derek: It was only after Mrs Hoffmann investigated herself that it was changed to murder?

Brigadier: Not according to what we have on the system.

Nicole: And eventually I got a copy of the docket. The docket had Inquest on it and it was registered, and then crossed out and written underneath Murder.

Lobo: A death inquest docket is when a person has maybe suddenly died from a medical cause and the police were alerted to the case. But there isn’t a lawful reason why an apparent obvious murder docket should be opened as an inquest.

Derek: We’ve been told by senior members that this was done to manipulate crime statistics.

Brigadier: Well I cannot confirm or deny that. We tried to check on the system, we couldn’t pick it up that it was ever registered as an inquest.

V/O: A glaring omission from the system and the docket is a charge of attempted murder on Nicole herself.

Lobo: So if there’s an attempted murder that occurred and wasn’t written up, then there’s definitely something wrong.

V/O: But this case is full of red flags. The investigating officer did not attend the post-mortem at the mortuary on the 27th of February. Three bullets were found in Piet’s body. The police only collected them 5 months later. The Forensic Officer also made a sworn affidavit that Body number 412, Piet’s body, was identified as being the body of one Marten Koekemoer.

Lobo: A body from a murder scene is evidence, although it gets buried or cremated afterwards, that is evidence and the chain of custody is in the hands of the investigating officer to make sure that the body number, the case number, the identity particulars of the deceased is all intact and correct in the docket.

V/O: But there was one more bullet that could have been used as evidence, found lodged in the engine of the Hoffmann’s car by the panel beater.

Nicole: I phoned and I phoned and I phoned and I said they are waiting for you to come and fetch the bullet. They are waiting, they are waiting. Nobody went to go and fetch it.

V/O: The day after the murder Nicole’s handbag was found at the Eufees Rd offramp in Pretoria. The police never did any forensics on the bag. Months later they located her stolen cellphone in Limpopo, but never went to get it.

Nicole: I was told by the person who has the docket currently, that do I realize if they go and get the phone, that most probably the person they have to arrest is not the perpetrator, and that’s very awkward.

Link: From an incorrect docket to not attending the post-mortem, to not collecting essential forensic evidence, it seems that Sandton police couldn’t even do the basics right to investigate Piet’s murder. Was it sheer incompetence, or deliberate bungling?

Brigadier: Like I said, shortcomings were picked up by one of our senior investigators who then escalated this docket to the Province where it is currently being investigated.

Derek: Can you understand Mrs Hoffmann’s frustration?

Brigadier: I’m sure she’s frustrated. I’m sure she’s traumatized after having gone through what she went through. But we want to assure her that we will do everything in our power to make sure that the suspects are apprehended and justice is served.

Nicole: Derek you don’t have closure. If at least an investigation was done I would feel like he could rest, and I could rest and our family could rest. But knowing everything that I know, I feel like there has been tampering with evidence and defeating the ends of justice from the authorities that are supposed to protect us.

So, we do not want to jeopardize this project. It’s big. Link: According to police crime statistics 58 people are murdered every day in South Africa. That means by next Sunday another 406 people will lose their lives. It’s a shocking reality, but what if the true figure is actually higher? What if all murders are not recorded as murders? V/O: A few months after Piet’s death Nicole phoned Sandton police station for some information. Nicole: And I said to her CAS 847, my husband’s murder. And she said but 847 case is not a murder. It’s registered as a robbery. Brigadier: Well from the information that we have Derek, two charges were registered on the case on the same day, just a minute apart. It was a robbery with firearm as well as a murder case. Derek: It was only after Mrs Hoffmann investigated herself that it was changed to murder? Brigadier: Not according to what we have on the system. Nicole: And eventually I got a copy of the docket. The docket had Inquest on it and it was registered, and then crossed out and written underneath Murder. Lobo: A death inquest docket is when a person has maybe suddenly died from a medical cause and the police were alerted to the case. But there isn’t a lawful reason why an apparent obvious murder docket should be opened as an inquest. Derek: We’ve been told by senior members that this was done to manipulate crime statistics. Brigadier: Well I cannot confirm or deny that. We tried to check on the system, we couldn’t pick it up that it was ever registered as an inquest. V/O: A glaring omission from the system and the docket is a charge of attempted murder on Nicole herself. Lobo: So if there’s an attempted murder that occurred and wasn’t written up, then there’s definitely something wrong. V/O: But this case is full of red flags. The investigating officer did not attend the post-mortem at the mortuary on the 27th of February. Three bullets were found in Piet’s body. The police only collected them 5 months later. The Forensic Officer also made a sworn affidavit that Body number 412, Piet’s body, was identified as being the body of one Marten Koekemoer. Lobo: A body from a murder scene is evidence, although it gets buried or cremated afterwards, that is evidence and the chain of custody is in the hands of the investigating officer to make sure that the body number, the case number, the identity particulars of the deceased is all intact and correct in the docket. V/O: But there was one more bullet that could have been used as evidence, found lodged in the engine of the Hoffmann’s car by the panel beater. Nicole: I phoned and I phoned and I phoned and I said they are waiting for you to come and fetch the bullet. They are waiting, they are waiting. Nobody went to go and fetch it. V/O: The day after the murder Nicole’s handbag was found at the Eufees Rd offramp in Pretoria. The police never did any forensics on the bag. Months later they located her stolen cellphone in Limpopo, but never went to get it. Nicole: I was told by the person who has the docket currently, that do I realize if they go and get the phone, that most probably the person they have to arrest is not the perpetrator, and that’s very awkward. Link: From an incorrect docket to not attending the post-mortem, to not collecting essential forensic evidence, it seems that Sandton police couldn’t even do the basics right to investigate Piet’s murder. Was it sheer incompetence, or deliberate bungling? Brigadier: Like I said, shortcomings were picked up by one of our senior investigators who then escalated this docket to the Province where it is currently being investigated. Derek: Can you understand Mrs Hoffmann’s frustration? Brigadier: I’m sure she’s frustrated. I’m sure she’s traumatized after having gone through what she went through. But we want to assure her that we will do everything in our power to make sure that the suspects are apprehended and justice is served. Nicole: Derek you don’t have closure. If at least an investigation was done I would feel like he could rest, and I could rest and our family could rest. But knowing everything that I know, I feel like there has been tampering with evidence and defeating the ends of justice from the authorities that are supposed to protect us. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Exclusive interview with widow who witnessed her husband's murder. Video footage of the incident
metadata.Summary: Pete & Nicola Hoffman lived in Durban. They were on business in Sandton on 26 February 2018, staying at the Hydro Executive Suites. They had dinner at Trumps in Nelson Mandela Square, where Pete posted it on Facebook. At 10.20pm they paid the bill and left the restaurant to drive back to their hotel in Grayston Drive. As they drove into the parking garage at 10:39pm they noticed there were no security guards on duty, and the boom was up - highly irregular for 24/7 security. They drove to the back of the underground parking, to the last parking next to the lifts. Pete reversed the Mercedes Benz Vito into the parking. As they opened their doors to get out a white Mercedes Benz sedan followed them into the garage and stopped a few metres away with its lights on. Three men got out carrying guns. Two of them ran up to Pete and shot him 7 times and stole his Rolex watch, gun and holster.t. A resident who heard the shots called SAPS and the ambulance. The security guards arrived on the scene 20 minutes later. Nic is now suing 24/7 security for R43 million. 12 days after Pete’s murder, on 7th March 2018, a special operation combining SAPS, Big Boyz Security and JMPD arrested a gang of armed robbers who had just hit a Clicks store in Midstream. The three men were arrested and taken to Midrand Police Station. The suspects in Midrand CAS 171/03/2018 1. Vusi Msimango 2. Sandile Skhosana 3. Tumelo Madubu On 9 March the suspects were fetched by Alexandra SAPS task team and taken to their homes in Alex, where a task team found 3 Rolex watches, a gun and holster, a Mercedes Benz key. A photograph was sent to Nicola of the stash – she recognized Pete’s watch – stopped at the exact time the murder took place – 10h40. When she later went to Alexandra SAPS, then Sandton SAPS to identify the watch, they brought out a different watch.
metadata.Further information: The Cover-Up 1. Sandton CAS 847/02/2018 is registered on the SAPS system as Robbery with Firearm. NO mention of Murder. This is done to massage crime statistics according to Captain Ben Booysen. 2. Forensic Officer gave sworn statement on 29 June 2018 that the body under CAS 847/02/2018 known as Body 412/2018 was identified by Tersia Robbetze as the body of Marten Koekemoer. But Koekemoer died and was cremated in Nov 2017. 3. SAPS officer not present at post-mortem. Bullets not collected for 5 months, subsequently lost, so no ballistics. 5 months to collect bullets found in bonnet of car by panel beater. But where are they? 4. No 205 done on Nicole’s phone for 7 months. Located in Limpopo, but never collected. Vodacom confirms the phone is still active. 5. No video footage collected from Trumps; only partial video footage 20” collected from Hydro, the remainder was wiped; 6. When Nicole contacted Peter Machlup, the 2nd hand Rolex dealer for a valuation of Pete’s watch he claimed to have no record of it. She subsequently found the invoice. Some of the Rolex Submariner’s advertised on his website do not have papers. So where does he get them from? 2 Years Later The docket has been with Detective Hennie Last since October 2018. Nicole thought he was with the Hawks. He is actually now a member of the Narcotics Unit. Nicole has written to Gauteng Provincial Commissioner 3 x asking for assistance. No reply.
